question: Side \(\overline{AB}\) of \(\triangle ABC\) has length \(10.\) The bisector of angle \(A\) meets \(\overline{BC}\) at \(D,\) and \(CD=3.\) The set of all possible values of \(AC\) is an open interval \((m, n).\) What is \(m+n?\)
solution:
The angle bisector lets us express the entire side \(BC\) in terms of \(AC\). Let \(q=AC>0\) and \(r=BD\). By the angle bisector theorem,
\[
\frac{q}{3}=\frac{10}{r},
\qquad r=\frac{30}{q}.
\]
Thus the three side lengths are \(q\), \(10\), and \(3+30/q\).

They form a nondegenerate triangle exactly when all three triangle inequalities hold. Multiplying each inequality by the positive number \(q\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
q+3+\frac{30}{q}>10
&\iff q^2-7q+30>0,\\
13+\frac{30}{q}>q
&\iff (q-15)(q+2)<0,\\
10+q>3+\frac{30}{q}
&\iff (q+10)(q-3)>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The first inequality always holds because
\[
q^2-7q+30=\left(q-\frac72\right)^2+\frac{71}{4}>0.
\]
Since \(q+2\) and \(q+10\) are positive, the other two inequalities give \(q<15\) and \(q>3\).

Conversely, every \(3<q<15\) gives positive side lengths satisfying all three triangle inequalities. The angle bisector then divides \(BC\) in the ratio \(BD:CD=10:q\), so
\[
CD=\left(3+\frac{30}{q}\right)\frac{q}{10+q}=3.
\]
Therefore the possible values of \(AC\) are exactly \((3,15)\), and
\[
m+n=3+15=\boxed{18}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
